title: The Corruption of the Earth and Human Wickedness
english: Of the Creator, for He is a support; and still, the removal of a number from Him makes a dyad, as it is evident that the three came by addition. But to humans, those things which are signified by the two, if a calculation were added, no longer remain material or human, partaking of rectitude; for it is not necessary merely to act, but also with right reason, so that it may receive praise.

And one is able, by changing the mode of speech, to take these things toward the perfection of the soul; for first a passion must come to the soul, then thus a disposition must become, and thus to impel toward action. And we say a passion is not the thing being denied, but the impulse of the soul as it would imprint upon the virtuous; and these things also happen from the opposite.

Three, therefore, are these offspring of the diligent; let the pre-passion now be as a weight toward the indifferent things. And if one, imposing [them] even upon interpretations, might find something useful, let him observe. Shem, indeed, is interpreted perfect, Japheth breadth or beauty, but Ham is daring or impetuous or heat or excess.

And what other offspring would have been fitting for the righteous, such as perfection, breadth and beauty, which are all the marks of virtue? For beauty, joined with breadth, makes the wide road go outward, which leads to destruction; but if it is that Ham is interpreted daring or impetuous or heat or excess, let these be taken as domestic to his manner, as if toward the worthless son for a reproach, but toward the perfect, let them be received with diligent use; for the virtuous is most unforced, since even the violent seize the kingdom; but such a one is also daring against the opposing powers, according to Paul the blessed saying, 'Our struggle is not against blood and flesh' (Eph 6:12), and the following: this impetuous one, just as he is daring, is not acquiring impetuousness toward evil, but happening upon virtue, being hot and zealous in the Spirit, from which he also stands apart from human [things] (Eph 1:11–12).
But the earth was against the Lord, and the earth was filled with injustice. And the Lord God saw the earth, and it was corrupted, because all flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth.

The corruption of the earth does not signify the loss of the so-beautiful element into non-existence, but rather the excess of the sins of men; the earth calls men by a metonymic manner, just as the psalmist says: 'Let all the earth worship you and sing to you' (Ps 66:5), and again 'Sing to the Lord, all the earth' (Ps 96:1); for when it is said 'The heavens and the earth were finished' (Gen 2:4), this element is signified, and 'Let the earth blossom' (Isa 45:18). Such has become the wickedness of men, who are called earth, as to see God, that element which incites them through much goodness and the great things of the wings. For it has been said: 'If, Lord, you observe iniquity, Lord, who will stand?' (Job 35:12). It does not bring wrath day by day, but when the moderate measures of sins occur, as it was said just as in the prophet Jonah: 'The cry of wickedness ascended to God' (Jon 2:2), and concerning Sodom: 'The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah has filled [the heavens], and their sins are exceedingly great' (Gen 18:20), just as here the similar is said: 'And the earth was filled with injustice' (Gen 6:11), and the rest.

See that [God] is not previously ignorant, but is manifesting the watchful power toward vengeance, just as in 'And God saw the earth, and it was corrupted' (Gen 6:11). And he calls the corruption the wickedness and the punishment upon it, just as the Scripture often declares in that which was said by Paul: 'If anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy him' (1 Cor 3:17); for he who, sinning through lawlessness, works the corruption of the temple of God, is found under punishment and is destroyed, the punishment being now signified by the corruption. And it is a corruption also to be delivered over to an unproven mind; for this is the most extreme punishment.
